exposure: Maternal age (advanced maternal age ≥ 35 years vs. < 35 years)
cohort: The study included all women with vaginally intended breech deliveries at the Department of Obstetrics and Perinatal Medicine at Goethe University Hospital in Frankfurt between January 2004 and December 2023.
finding: Maternal age of 35 years or older was not linked to higher perinatal morbidity following vaginally attempted breech delivery, but was significantly associated with a higher rate of cesarean section and, in vaginally completed deliveries, higher odds of postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Advanced maternal age was significantly associated with a higher rate of cesarean section in vaginally intended breech deliveries.
